issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s prior non-eviction protection under a repealed rent-control law does not bar protection under the successor law when the tenant makes the successor law’s required rent deposit.
material_facts: The tenants had obtained non-eviction protection under the earlier rent-control law in eviction proceedings that were pending when the successor law came into force; the saving clause required those proceedings to be disposed of under the earlier law.
After a later rent default, the landlords brought eviction proceedings under the successor law, and the tenants made the rent deposit required in those proceedings.
The tenants had not previously obtained the successor law’s non-eviction protection.
issues.conclusion: The earlier protection under the repealed law did not trigger the successor law’s bar on obtaining its non-eviction protection. The tenants were entitled to that protection, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(2) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 grants non-eviction protection when a tenant makes the payment or deposit required by section 15; its proviso bars a further benefit only where the tenant has already obtained that benefit under section 14(2). Under section 57(2), proceedings pending under the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952 when the 1958 Act commenced were to continue under the earlier Act, so a deposit in those proceedings was a deposit under section 13(2) of the 1952 Act, not section 15 of the 1958 Act. The Court applied the grammatical construction of clear statutory language, approved Dhan Raj Jayna v. S.P. Singh, AIR 1973 Delhi 297, and noted the material differences between the earlier and successor schemes; J.K. Steel Ltd. v. Union of India, [1969] 2 SCR 481, 497, did not establish that the provisions were in pari materia.

rule.if: successor_law_rent_default_eviction_case and required_successor_law_deposit and prior_saved_proceeding_relief_under_earlier_law and no_prior_successor_law_relief

predicates.successor_law_rent_default_eviction_case: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding under a successor rent-control regime based on a tenant’s rent default.
predicates.required_successor_law_deposit: The tenant made the rent payment or deposit required for protection in the successor-law proceeding.
predicates.prior_saved_proceeding_relief_under_earl: The tenant had previously avoided eviction under an earlier rent-control regime in a proceeding pending when the successor regime began.
predicates.no_prior_successor_law_relief: The tenant had not previously obtained non-eviction protection under the successor rent-control regime.

issues.definition: When a tenant makes the required deposit in a successor-regime rent-default eviction case, earlier protection in a saved proceeding under the former regime does not prevent the tenant from receiving the successor regime’s non-eviction protection if the tenant has not previously received that successor-regime protection.
